The NCS said an earthquake of magnitude 4.9 struck Chamoli in Uttarakhand at 10:22 pm IST.

stories.headline: CM Samrat Choudhary directs officials to submit detailed report on flood damage in Bihar
stories.title: CM Samrat Choudhary directs officials to submit detailed report on flood damage in Bihar
stories.summary: He instructed that the Disaster Management Department must obtain assessments of flood damage and rehabilitation costs from all relevant departments and submit a report at the earliest.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) directed officials concerned to immediately submit a detailed report of damages due to flood in Bihar.

He issued the direction during a review meeting in which Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) National President Nitin Nabin and both Deputy Chief Ministers of Bihar Vijay Kumar Choudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav were present along with other officials.
Mr. Choudhary said that a severe flood situation arose this year due to an unprecedented volume of water flowing into the Ganga, Gandak, and Son rivers compared to previous years.
He pointed out that the accumulation of silt in riverbeds is a primary reason for river flooding.
He added that Bihar is the first State in the country to have formulated a silt policy.
The Chief Minister directed that the current status of rivers and the damage caused by floods be continuously monitored.

“A detailed preliminary report on the flood damage should be submitted immediately so that relief, rehabilitation, and necessary development works in the affected areas can be expedited, “Mr. Choudhary said.
He also instructed the DMD to obtain assessments of the flood damage and the costs required for restoration from all concerned departments and submit a report at the earliest.
Mr. Choudhary also directed that necessary arrangements be ensured to address potential issues arising after the drainage of water from the flood-affected areas.
He mentioned that in the second phase, compensation amounts would be transferred to the flood-affected families on October 12, 2026.
Chandrashekhar Singh, Secretary of the Water Resources Department (WRD), briefed about the causes and situation arising from the two phases of flooding in Bihar.
He explained that during the first phase, new peak water levels were recorded in the Ganga, Son, Ghaghara, Kosi, and Punpun rivers, surpassing previous highs.

stories.headline: SP decides not a field a third candidate for the Rajya Sabha election
stories.title: SP decides not a field a third candidate for the Rajya Sabha election
stories.summary: The focus is on the Assembly election, Akhilesh Yadav says, with the party preparing to contest all the Assembly seats
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Samajwadi Party (SP) on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) decided not to field a third candidate for the forthcoming Rajya Sabha election, paving the way for all 10 seats from Uttar Pradesh to be filled without a contest.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the SP engaged in political slugfest over the development, with the ruling BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) ridiculing the Opposition party, while the SP hit back to say the real target was the Assembly election in early 2027.

“Now our focus is not on three (Rajya Sabha nominations), but on 403 (the number of seats in the U.P. Assembly),” Mr. Yadav said on social media platform X, with the party deciding to focus its energy on the forthcoming Assembly election, having analysed the current political situation.
The SP national president’s post made it clear that the party was preparing to contest all Assembly seats.

“Our national president made it clear again and again that the number of seats was not the issue but the winnability of candidates with the objective of forming the government in 2027 by defeating the BJP,” senior SP leader Sudhir Panwar said.

The SP was not going to boycott the Assembly election due to the controversies surrounding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Mr. Panwar said, adding, “People will throw out both the BJP and the Chief Election Commissioner in the near future.”
The SP has nominated senior leader Ram Gopal Yadav and industrialist Dhanraj Nathwani as its candidates in the Rajya Sabha election.
Earlier last week, Mr. Yadav had indicated the party would contest three seats.
The SP has eight fewer MLAs than it needs to have a third member elected.
U.P. Minister of Panchayati Raj Om Prakash Rajbhar targeted the SP on social media platform X. “My friend Akhilesh, it’s all done, just snap.
Well, sometimes, even if it’s just a matter of time, you still do something sensible.
Like you did today.

stories.headline: Congress steps up agitation for removal of Chief Election Commissioner
stories.title: Congress steps up agitation for removal of Chief Election Commissioner
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Transport and BC Welfare Minister Ponnam Prabhakar on Tuesday warned that the Congress would not remain silent if eligible voters were denied their fundamental right to vote, even as Telangana Youth Congress cadres staged a protest outside the State Chief Electoral Officer’s office here demanding the removal and arrest of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Speaking to the media at Sriramulapalli in Koheda mandal of Siddipet district, Mr. Prabhakar alleged that votes of poor and eligible people in rural areas were being removed in the name of revision of electoral rolls.
He accused the Election Commission of India (ECI) failing to function independently and alleged that it was acting under the influence of the Centre.

He condemned the detention of Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi during their protest in Delhi against alleged irregularities in the electoral process, describing the action as undemocratic.
He said the Congress would intensify its ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ campaign from the village level to protect the voting rights of every citizen.
Meanwhile, Telangana Youth Congress president Jakkidi Shiva Charan Reddy led the protest outside the Telangana CEO’s office and demanded his immediate arrest.
Mr. Reddy alleged that the CEC was acting in the interests of the BJP and RSS and claimed that nearly 14 crore votes had been removed across the country without due procedure.
He said the Youth Congress would organise protests across Telangana seeking the resignation of Mr. Kumar.
He warned that the agitation would be intensified if the Centre failed to respond to their demands.
Separately, leaders of INDIA bloc parties staged a protest outside the Hyderabad Collectorate demanding the removal and arrest of Mr. Kumar.
They submitted a representation to the Joint Collector and said their agitation would continue until the CEC was removed and a thorough investigation ordered.

Meanwhile, Congress Khairatabad district president M. Rohit, Secunderabad district president Deepak Jain, MLC Kodandaram, CPI State leader Narasimha, CPI(M) city secretary Venkatesh, Telangana Jana Samithi (TJS) leaders Salim Pasha and Arun Kumar, Hyderabad district president Narsaiah and representatives of the VCK participated in the protest.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Reserves Judgment On Pleas Against Delhi HC Verdict Diluting Mandatory Attendance Requirement For Law Students
stories.title: Supreme Court Reserves Judgment On Pleas Against Delhi HC Verdict Diluting Mandatory Attendance Requirement For Law Students
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Tuesday reserved judgment on pleas challenging the Delhi High Court's November 2025 ruling that law students cannot be barred from appearing in examinations or continuing their academic pursuits solely on account of shortage of attendance.

A bench of Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Sandeep Mehta and Justice Augustine George Masih reserved the verdict in pleas filed by Bar Council of India (BCI) and Narsi Monjee Institute of Management Studies (NMIMS) challenging the High Court judgment which also directed BCI to reconsider mandatory attendance requirements for three-year and five-year LL.B. courses.
The Delhi High Court passed the impugned judgment in a suo motu proceeding arising from the suicide of a student of Amity Law School, Delhi, in 2016.
The High Court held that attendance requirements in legal education could not be enforced so rigidly that they resulted in mental trauma or contributed to extreme consequences such as suicide.

It held that no student enrolled in a recognised law college, university or institution in India could be detained from taking an examination or prevented from further academic pursuits or career progression on the ground of lack of minimum attendance.
It also held that institutions could not prescribe attendance norms above the minimum percentage fixed by the BCI.

The High Court observed that legal education cannot be reduced to classroom attendance, as students also require practical exposure through moot courts, seminars, Parliament debates, court hearings, legal aid clinics and other activities.
It held that sufficient flexibility in attendance norms was necessary to enable students to participate in such activities and obtain "multi-dimensional learning and training".

The High Court also referred to the National Education Policy, 2020 and the UGC framework, observing that the approach to education had moved towards flexibility, multidisciplinary learning and greater use of online modes of education.

The High Court directed BCI to undertake a re-evaluation of mandatory attendance norms for three-year and five-year LL.B. courses after stakeholder consultations involving students, student bodies, parents and teachers.
It directed the BCI to consider giving credit for activities such as moot courts, seminars, Parliament debates and attending court hearings.
Pending that exercise, the High Court prescribed an interim regime.

opening: The Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI’s) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) will announce its October policy decision on Wednesday.
A Reuters poll of 61 economists has found that 35 expect a 25-basis-point hike.
body: If delivered, it would mark the RBI’s first rate increase since February 2023.
The repo rate—the rate at which the RBI lends to banks—has remained at 5.25 percent for the past four meetings, following 125 basis points of cuts in 2025.
Last MPC meeting: Key takeawaysRepo rate: Held at 5.25 percent for the fourth consecutive meeting.
The MPC unanimously retained its neutral stance.
Inflation: RBI cut its FY27 CPI inflation forecast to 5 percent from 5.1 percent, but said higher fuel and food prices were largely supply-driven and inflation had not yet become broad-based.
Brent crude has also risen above $100 a barrel, while the rupee remains under pressure.
The US Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan also raised rates by 25 bps in September.

SBI Research, in its MPC preview, said the “balance of risks has tilted decisively towards a 25-bps rate hike”, citing broader inflation pressures, worsening global conditions and renewed repricing of risks in financial markets.
How much further could rates rise?
Nomura expects only 25-50 basis points of increases, arguing that inflation has not yet become broadly entrenched and that growth could weaken.
Meanwhile, Bank of America, ANZ and Goldman Sachs expect a larger 75-100 basis-point cycle, reflecting stronger growth and wider inflation pressures, according to a report by Reuters.

Shriram Research, in its monthly policy preview, said “the case for an extended tightening cycle is weak”, citing the risks to growth from higher oil prices, weaker rural demand and rate-sensitive investment.
The RBI’s updated inflation and growth forecasts, and any change to its “neutral” policy stance, will offer clues on how it sees the path ahead.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves five commissionerates for Bengaluru; former officers express concern
stories.title: Cabinet approves five commissionerates for Bengaluru; former officers express concern
stories.summary: Former senior police officers have questioned whether a civic structure can be directly replicated in policing, arguing that crime, law and order, traffic management and emergency mobilisation do not necessarily follow municipal boundaries
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Karnataka Cabinet on Tuesday approved the reorganisation of the Bengaluru police commissionerate into five commissionerates, with a Chief.
Police Commissioner to oversee them.
The proposed overhaul has triggered a sharp debate among serving and retired police officials.

The restructuring has been proposed against the backdrop of Bengaluru’s rapid expansion and the creation of the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), which has divided the civic administration into five corporations.
The proposed police model broadly seeks to mirror this arrangement to improve coordination between the police and civic authorities.

However, former senior police officers have questioned whether a civic structure can be directly replicated in policing, arguing that crime, law and order, traffic management and emergency mobilisation do not necessarily follow municipal boundaries.
A former DGP who served in the Bengaluru city police said the proposed arrangement could create more problems than solutions, particularly in operational policing.

According to the former officer, the proposal appears to be driven partly by the desire to “accommodate senior officials seeking postings in major metropolitan centres rather than by a clearly established operational requirement”.

The former DGP said the present city police structure has a clearly defined chain of command involving the Commissioner of Police, DCPs, inspectors and constables, with responsibilities and jurisdictions understood at every level.
The proposed five-commissionerate system, he argued, could dilute this established structure by creating multiple command centres and overlapping responsibilities.
“The existing system has a clear chain of command.
The new arrangement could make these established positions less significant and create confusion at different levels,” the former officer said.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority for greater efficiency
stories.title: Cabinet approves Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority for greater efficiency
stories.summary: Seeks to address long-standing challenges; strengthen research, planning, appraisal, monitoring
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday approved the setting up of a special purpose vehicle (SPV) — Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA) - to strengthen research, planning, appraisal, monitoring and impact assessment of transportation and logistics.

“The approval seeks to address the long-standing challenges arising from fragmented planning and implementation across multiple transport-related Ministries and agencies,” per a statement issued by the government.

A long-term transport plan covering roads, railways, ports and shipping, civil aviation, inland waterways, coastal shipping, urban mobility and logistics, will be prepared by the ITLA, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said at a media briefing following the Cabinet meeting.
The ITLA is expected to enhance the efficiency, sustainability and effectiveness of transport infrastructure development in India by fostering greater coordination and multi-modal integration.

“ITLA will prepare a comprehensive National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of ten years or more, covering roads, railways, ports and shipping, civil aviation, inland waterways, coastal shipping, urban mobility and logistics,” the statement highlighted.

It will evaluate short-term sectoral plans (five years or so) and annual plans of transport Ministries to ensure consistency and alignment with the National Transport Master Plan and promote multi-modal infrastructure development.

It will undertake technical appraisal of infrastructure projects of government, costing ₹500 crore or more, while financial appraisal will continue to be carried out through the existing financial appraisal mechanisms.

ITLA will also build a National Transport Data Repository, integrating datasets including GSTN e-way bills, FASTag, Vahan, GPS and urban traffic systems for freight-flow and origin-destination analytics.
It will advise on the review and updation of the National Logistics Policy, support capacity building, training and skilling, and promote research and innovation in transport and logistics.

The institution is expected to strengthen multimodal connectivity, improve infrastructure efficiency, reduce logistics costs and enhance India’s global logistics competitiveness as part of Vision 2047.

ITLA will also build a National Transport Data Repository, integrating datasets including GSTN e-way bills, FASTag, Vahan, GPS and urban traffic systems for freight-flow and origin-destination analytics.
It will advise on the review and updation of the National Logistics Policy, support capacity building, training and skilling, and promote research and innovation in transport and logistics.

The institution is expected to strengthen multimodal connectivity, improve infrastructure efficiency, reduce logistics costs and enhance India’s global logistics competitiveness as part of Vision 2047.
